title: Console analytics star-schema and retention strategy
creator: Rina Patel
description: Design and deliver a curated, production-ready star-schema for Console usage and cost analytics. Goal is to provide fast, low-cost analytical queries for product, finance, and SRE teams: session-level usage, token breakdown by route/model, user/org cost attribution, and event-level traces needed for billing reconciliation. Work includes schema design, partitioning and clustering strategy, retention policy, materialized tables/aggregates, and migration plan from existing ad-hoc staging tables.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical star-schema tables implemented in the warehouse (facts: console_events_fact, token_usage_fact; dimensions: user_dim, org_dim, model_dim, route_dim)
Queries for top-10 analytics use cases return within SLA (95th percentile < 3s on BI slots) using curated tables
Retention and cost model defined and enforced (hot partitions 90 days, cold aggregates 13 months), with clear recompute cadence
Backfill plan and migration runbook documented and validated in staging with sample datasets
Dashboards updated to point at curated tables; sample BI queries and example SQL saved in docs repository
implementation_plan: Week 1: Finalize star-schema model and partitioning strategy with Data Platform (design doc + ER diagram)
Week 2: Implement ETL/ELT pipelines (dbt models) to populate dimension tables and incremental facts using event stream snapshots
Week 3: Add materialized monthly/weekly aggregates, configure scheduled recompute jobs and monitor cost impact
Week 4: Run backfill for last 18 months in staging, validate row counts and reconciliations with raw events
Week 5: Cutover dashboards, enable replication to reporting project, and monitor query latencies and costs for two weeks
progress_updates: 2026-02-27: Kickoff - aligned PM and Data Platform on scope; confirmed top analytics personas and 12 canonical queries
2026-03-02: Chose star-schema over normalized snowflake to optimize BI latency; trade-off: slightly larger storage for faster joins
2026-03-04: Decided on BigQuery as primary warehouse for Console analytics due to existing billing datasets and BI integration; validated partition/cluster options
2026-03-07: Implemented initial user_dim, org_dim, and model_dim dbt models (PR open) - awaiting Data Platform review
2026-03-10: Proof-of-concept token_usage_fact shows 4x faster average query time versus ad-hoc staging tables on sample dataset
review_feedback: PM (Eli Johnson): emphasize API route-level attribution for per-route cost visibility; add route_dim and ensure route tags are stable
Data Platform (Sofia Morales): recommend hourly incremental load with micro-partitions to keep streaming costs low; avoid frequent full-table rewrites
Security (Ana Gomez): ensure PII-free user_dim by storing hashed user_id and keeping raw identifiers only in secure audit logs
Finance (Oliver Grant): request currency-normalized cost column and daily exchange-rate join for cross-region billing comparisons
linked_dashboards: Looker: Console > Usage Overview - now pointing to curated tables (pending PR)
Grafana: Console Query Latency (sample job) - instrumentation added to ETL jobs
Metabase: Cost by Route - to be migrated after backfill
prs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/559 - grant BI service account read access to reporting dataset
risk_mitigation: Start with conservative retention (90 days hot) and measure storage growth before enabling 13-month cold aggregates
Smoke tests and row-count reconciliation to detect ETL drift; add alerting when reconciliation fails > 0.5%
Stagger backfill jobs to limit peak egress and slot usage; use partitioned windowing and sampling for validation
Fallback: keep existing staging tables readable for 4 weeks post-cutover to allow rollback of dashboards
notes: Consider adding small pre-aggregates for high-cardinality metrics (per-org-per-model daily) to reduce scan costs
Explore using materialized views for monthly billing summary to accelerate finance reports
Long-term: evaluate pushing lightweight pre-aggregation into runtime (edge cache) for fastest 95th percentile queries
